problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=5-t \\ y=4+2t \\ z=-6-3t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:4x+6y-3z-130=0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Intersection Between a Line and a Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line in Parametric Form and a Plane in Cartesian Form

Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14059450/assets/2a24a49f0fc47c235776597df655e75be9c68cffbb7988db16b36d9200f801bc.png)
examples.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+4y+6z+25 & =0 \\ 3(3-4t)+4(-1+2t)+6(2+3t)+25 & =0 \\ 9-12t-4+8t+12+18t+25 & =0 \\ 14t & =-42 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-4(-3)=15 \\ y=-1+2(-3)=-7 \\ z=2+3(-3)=-7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(15,-7,-7).$

feedback.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨5,-2,3⟩+t⟨0,3,-1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩=-7.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ ⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ 5+3(-2+3t)+(-2)(3-t) & =-7 \\ 5-6+9t-6+2t & =-7 \\ 11t & =0 \\ t & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=0$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5,-2+3(0),3-0⟩ \\  & =⟨5,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5,-2,3).$
